defects.title: CubeView.daily("ListAge") is anchored to the VIEW's first day, not the store's — on any windowed/warmed view the plane is cross-sectionally constant and the same stock-day's age disagrees with the full view by ~10000
defects.failure_scenario:
Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a9_listage_view_anchored.py (10 symbols x 60 days, unlisted_days=8, so the last symbol lists on store day 8).

  st.view().daily("ListAge")                        -> store day 30: young symbol 22.0, old symbol 10030.0  (2 distinct values in the cross-section)
  st.view(start=dates[20]).daily("ListAge")         -> the SAME store day 30: young symbol 10010.0, old symbol 10010.0  (1 distinct value)
  warmed_view(st, start=dates[30], end=dates[50], warmup=10).daily("ListAge") -> store day 30 column is [10010.]*10  (1 distinct value)

Two consequences, both silent:
(1) The same (symbol, date) cell gets 22.0 in one view and 10010.0 in another, so a factor containing ListAge mined under research/mining (windowed) and then exported by calculate (different window) produces different numbers for the same day — the "plausible-looking wrong number" the design's own risks section is about. contract_hash does not change with the window, so nothing flags it.
(2) Every symbol listed before the window's first day gets LIST_AGE_SENTINEL + d, so on a windowed view the plane is constant across the cross-section: cs_rank(ListAge) / cs_zscore(ListAge) are a flat tie / all-zero, i.e. any ListAge factor silently carries zero information. This is the normal case, not an edge case: pipeline.py:244, research.py:111 and calculate.py:126 all build their view via warmed_view(store, start, end, ...), and calculate.py:210 via store.view(start=..., end=...).

This contradicts the design's stated definition (section "New module src/alphacube/dailyfields.py": "LIST_AGE_SENTINEL for a stock already listed on the STORE's first day") and it is the one field for which the design's own WP3 test bullet "view independence … equals the full-view plane indexed by that subset" fails. The deviation is not listed in the commit's deviations, and tests/test_daily_fields_store.py:382 (the only ListAge test) uses the full-view `daily_view` fixture, so it is blind to it.
defects.suggested_fix:
Anchor the lifecycle counter to the store, then slice to the window, inside CubeView.daily() — the one place that knows both axes. E.g. special-case the lifecycle-dependent field before the generic resolve call at store.py:539-541:

    if name == "ListAge":
        rows = self._rows(0, self.n_symbols)
        full_status = self.store.read_status(rows, 0, self.store.n_days)
        plane = resolve(name, self.symbols, self.store.dates, store=self.store.daily, status=full_status)
        self._daily[name] = np.ascontiguousarray(plane[:, self.d0:self.d1])
    else:
        self._daily[name] = resolve(name, self.symbols, self.dates, ...)

(Equivalently: give dailyfields.derive a `day_offset`/`first_date_index` argument so the sticky cumsum starts at the store's day 0.) That costs one extra (S_view x D_store) int8 read per view, is identical on a full view (so tests/test_daily_fields_store.py:382 stays green), and makes ListAge satisfy the same view-independence property as FloatCap/LimitWidth/BoardCode. Then extend the ListAge test to assert exactly that: `st.view(start=dates[20]).daily("ListAge") == st.view().daily("ListAge")[:, 20:]`.

defects.title: The contract_hash backward-compatibility tests only pin self-consistency, not byte-identity — they stay green under the exact break design item 7 forbids
defects.failure_scenario:
test_contract_hash_is_byte_identical_without_a_daily_source asserts `CubeStore(store.directory).contract_hash == store.contract_hash`, i.e. that two stores built by the SAME code agree. That is true for any implementation. Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a1_contract_hash_vs_baseline.py

  BASE (517fd09) CubeStore.contract_hash = d84654d39c61212758746044bf35bf36947243b7d2433e01c0b0cae7d04d9c02
  STEER          CubeStore.contract_hash = d84654d39c61212758746044bf35bf36947243b7d2433e01c0b0cae7d04d9c02   <- correct today
  had `parts["daily"] = fingerprint(self.daily)` been added UNCONDITIONALLY (fingerprint returns None with no daily source):
                                            2b5d77b241bc23510accd0c3c370467c255ede2198da1a79a93ba4f1d7b1b4b0
  the test's own assertion under that variant: True   <- still passes

So a one-character change that invalidates every stored contract_hash on the server (calculate.py:174 records it; Partura's PanelSet.view_id is about to mix it in per the design) is not caught by any test. test_contract_hash_unchanged_and_changed_for_a_two_segment_segmented_store (line 186) has the same hole for SegmentedCubeStore, and the only other guard, tests/test_store_layouts.py:50, asserts `seg.contract_hash != mono.contract_hash`, which an added key does not break either. The implementation is correct; the guard is not.
defects.suggested_fix: Pin the literal pre-WP3 payload rather than self-consistency. In test_contract_hash_is_byte_identical_without_a_daily_source add `from alphacube.store import canonical_hash` and `assert store.contract_hash == canonical_hash({"meta_sha256": store.meta_sha256})`. In the segmented test add `assert set(plain_a.contract) == {"base_minute_meta_sha256", "index_sha256", "segment_meta_sha256"}` and `assert plain_a.contract_hash == canonical_hash(plain_a.contract)` before the daily root is attached. Both go red if the "daily" key ever becomes unconditional.

defects.title: resolve()'s float32 cast destroys the identifiable plane's date component (+d), so the warmed_view date-padding half of the view-independence test is vacuous
defects.failure_scenario:
FloatCap[s, d] = 1e9*(s+1) + d is identifiable in float64, but CubeView.daily() returns float32, where the spacing at 1e9/5e9/1e10 is 64/512/1024 — far larger than d (0..59). Measured (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a2_identifiable_plane_float32.py):

  float64 distinct values per symbol row: [60]*10
  float32 distinct values per symbol row: [2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1]

So each row is (almost) constant along the date axis and no view-level test built on this fixture can see a date-axis alignment error. Sabotaging DailyFieldStore.align to index the DATE axis by POSITION instead of by label (exactly the bug the identifiable values are advertised to expose) and re-running the test bodies:

  --- SABOTAGED date axis ---
    PASS  test_view_independence_symbol_subset_and_warmed_view_padding
    PASS  test_daily_view_float_cap_matches_the_identifiable_plane_exactly
    FAIL  test_daily_nan_fills_exactly_...   (its values are 1e9 apart, so it is the only one that notices)

test_view_independence_symbol_subset_and_warmed_view_padding exists precisely to pin the design's claim that "warmed_view's backward-extended d0 lines up for free"; its symbol half is real (a positional symbol bug does turn it red), but its date half asserts nothing — the padded view starts 10 days earlier and the test still passes.
defects.suggested_fix: Make the date term survive float32: scale it in synthetic.make_synthetic_cube (store.py is unaffected), e.g. `float_cap = 1e9*(s+1) + 1e6*d` — still ~1e9 magnitude, still 'identifiable by POSITION', but 1e6 is far above the float32 spacing of 64..1024, so both axes are distinguishable (keep TotalCap/FloatShares as the same ratios and update test_identifiable_planes_formula_and_relationships). If the design's literal `+ d` must be kept, instead add a date assertion that cannot be satisfied by a constant row, e.g. compare `padded.daily("FloatCap")` against `np.float32(st.daily.align("FloatCap", padded.symbols, padded.dates))` computed from the float64 plane, or assert `padded.daily("FloatCap")[:, 0] != st.view().daily("FloatCap")[idx, 0]` is impossible only because the dates genuinely coincide.

defects.title: ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS="" makes open_cube_store raise FileNotFoundError instead of behaving as unset
defects.failure_scenario: `daily_root = os.environ.get("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS")` returns "" (not None) for an exported-but-empty variable, so `if daily_root is not None` is True and DailyFieldStore(Path("")) looks for ./meta.json. Repro (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a3_misc_edges.py): with ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS set to "", `open_cube_store(store.directory)` raises `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'meta.json'`. `ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS= python -m alphacube.cli mine ...` and `export ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS=""` in a sweep script are the ordinary ways to turn an env knob off, and the design names this variable as "the env equivalent for sweep scripts" (WP8). The sibling knob two lines down uses truthiness (`Path(mirror_dir) if mirror_dir else None`), so the two disagree.
defects.suggested_fix: `daily_root = os.environ.get("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS") or None` at store.py:445, and extend test_open_cube_store_env_var_default_and_direct_construction_ignores_it with `monkeypatch.setenv("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS", ""); assert open_cube_store(mono.directory).daily is None`.

defects.title: daily() passes the raw status plane to a helper that hardcodes OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE == 0, bypassing the store's own day_status_codes map
defects.failure_scenario: CubeStore builds `self._codes = {**DAY_STATUS_CODES, **self.meta.get("day_status_codes", {})}` so a store may legitimately remap the codes, and every other reader honours that map (CubeStore.tradable():189, SegmentedCubeStore.read_status():420 fills with `self._codes["OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE"]`, CubeView.tradable():486 reads `getattr(self.store, "_codes", ...)`). CubeView.daily() hands `status=self.day_status()` straight to dailyfields._lifecycle_mask, which tests `status != _OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE` with `_OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE = 0` hardcoded (dailyfields.py:86). On a store whose meta declares e.g. `{"OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE": 9}`, every not-yet-listed stock-day is read as in-lifecycle, so ListAge silently reports the sentinel for a stock that had not listed yet — no error, no warning. No store in the tree remaps the codes today, which is why the suite is green; the meta key exists precisely to allow it.
defects.suggested_fix: Translate at the boundary, where the code map is in hand. In CubeView.daily(), pass a lifecycle boolean instead of a raw code plane: `codes = getattr(self.store, "_codes", DAY_STATUS_CODES)` then `status=None, tradable=(self.day_status() != codes["OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE"])` — _lifecycle_mask's `tradable` branch already means exactly "True counts toward ListAge". (Alternatively give dailyfields.resolve an `outside_lifecycle=0` keyword and pass `codes["OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE"]`.) Add a test that builds a store via build_cube_store(..., extra_meta={"day_status_codes": {...remapped...}}) and checks ListAge still NaNs the unlisted prefix.

defects.title: daily_s/daily_d hand out writable views into the per-view cache, unlike read_s/read_d which copy
defects.failure_scenario: `return self.daily(name)[s_lo:s_hi, :]` is a basic numpy slice, so it aliases the cached plane and is writable. Measured (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a3_misc_edges.py): `np.shares_memory(view.daily_s("FloatCap", 0, 3), view.daily("FloatCap")) is True`, `writeable is True`, and writing to the slice leaves the cached plane permanently corrupted (`view.daily("FloatCap")[0, :3] -> [-1. -1. -1.]`) for every later chunk and every later consuming edge in the same view. read_s/read_d return a fresh `np.array(..., copy=True)` per call, so the engine has never had to care. WP4 is told to use daily_s/daily_d "exactly as read_s/read_d are used today" and will wrap them in `torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(sl))`; for MODE_S the ascontiguousarray is a no-op and `.to(cpu, float32)` returns the same tensor, so the tensor aliases the cache. Nothing mutates a leaf in place today (I grepped src/alphacube/operators for in-place torch ops and every hit writes to a freshly allocated output), so this is latent rather than live — but it is a silent-wrong-numbers failure mode if it ever stops being true, and it costs one line to close.
defects.suggested_fix: Freeze the cache once, in daily(): `arr = resolve(...); arr.setflags(write=False); self._daily[name] = arr`. An accidental in-place write then raises ValueError instead of corrupting the plane, and WP4's `np.ascontiguousarray` + `torch.from_numpy` still works (it only emits torch's non-writable-array UserWarning, which this suite already carries elsewhere). If you would rather avoid that warning, have daily_s/daily_d return `np.array(self.daily(name)[...], copy=True)` and drop the "thin slice" wording from the docstrings.

result.notes:
WORKTREE / HYGIENE: reviewed /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering at cc6619b on branch partura-steering; working tree clean before and after (I changed no tracked file, committed nothing, pushed nothing, opened no network connection). All attack scripts live in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/ (a1_contract_hash_vs_baseline.py, a2_identifiable_plane_float32.py, a3_misc_edges.py, a9_listage_view_anchored.py). a1 reads the baseline tree /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube read-only via PYTHONPATH.

FILES TOUCHED (2e): `git show --name-only` = exactly the four owned files plus tests/test_store_layouts.py. That fifth file is the declared deviation and the edit is the minimal one (four-value unpack -> five, binding `_daily_planes`). I re-ran the grep: in-tree there is no other direct make_synthetic_cube caller with a fixed four-value unpack; scripts/ only ever uses write_synthetic_store (validate_gpu_parity.py:182, compare_daily_store.py:116), which was updated. I also grepped /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura and /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura-steering for make_synthetic_cube / write_synthetic_store / "SH.6" — zero hits, so the 4->5 arity break and the symbol-spelling break are contained inside this repo.

DESIGN COVERAGE (2a): every WP3 step is present with the design's signatures — CubeStore(directory, mirror_dir=None, daily_root=None); SegmentedCubeStore(compute_root, include_segments=True, mirror_root=None, daily_root=None); open_cube_store(path, include_segments=True, mirror_root=None, daily_root=None) with the $ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS default; CubeView._daily, daily_fields property, daily(name), daily_s(name, lo, hi), daily_d(name, lo, hi); the (S, D)-not-(D, S) documentation; the symbol respelling; make_synthetic_cube(daily_fields=()) with the fifth element; write_daily_fields; the two conftest fixtures. Two harmless loosenings of design prose: the fifth element is UNCONDITIONAL rather than "keyword-gated" (the right call — it is what keeps write_synthetic_store's arity stable, and the commit says so), and _synthetic_symbols gives n-3 main-board symbols rather than the design's "first two thirds". DailyFeature exposes `.field` (expression.py:155), so WP4's `view.daily_s(expr.field, lo, hi)` connects as designed.

DEFAULT-PATH / RNG IDENTITY (2b): verified branch by branch, not taken on faith.
- make_synthetic_cube: the only new branch is `if daily_fields:` at synthetic.py:129, after every rng draw (last draw is line 119); the planes are pure index arithmetic on np.arange, and `rng` is function-local so there is nothing downstream to perturb. Stream identity is structural, not just asserted by the test.
- CubeStore/SegmentedCubeStore: both new blocks are gated on `daily_root is not None` and neither constructor reads the environment (confirmed in source and by test:220).
- contract_hash: byte-identity against the pre-WP3 code measured directly, same store directory, both trees — d84654d3…4d9c02 on both. See defect 2 for why no test pins this.
- tradable(): the refactor to derive from the new day_status() is textually equivalent (`np.isin(<same array>, [TRADING, RESUMED])`); the only cost is that the (S, D) int8 plane is now retained for the view's lifetime (~10 MB on the 5219x1942 production store), which is noise next to the (S, D) float32 daily cache the same view will hold (~40 MB per resolved field, up to 9 fields — worth knowing for WP4's device cache budget, not a defect).
- Full suite: 762 passed / 10 skipped / 1 xfailed, exactly the commit's claimed count; 41 tests collected from tests/test_daily_fields_store.py, matching "+41 from this package's new file". Zero new failures.

LOWER-PRIORITY OBSERVATIONS (not filed as defects):
- _synthetic_symbols docstring says "as many of them are kept as fit (main board first)" for n < 3, but the code keeps the SPECIALS and drops the main board: n=1 -> ['688001.SH'], n=2 -> ['688001.SH', '300001.SZ']. Nothing in the suite builds a store that small; it is a docstring/code mismatch worth one word ("special boards first").
- A legitimately main-board-only view (store.view(max_symbols=4), or warmed_view(symbols=[...600xxx...])) emits dailyfields' RuntimeWarning on every LimitWidth/BoardCode resolve. Measured; it is by WP2's design (the format half raises, the composition half only warns) and Python de-duplicates it per process, so it is noise rather than breakage — but research/evaluate_factors with max_symbols is a common smoke path and WP8 should expect the line in run logs.
- The symbol respelling is a deliberate behaviour change beyond the tests: the synthetic fixture's board limits go from a uniform 0.10 to {0.10, 0.20, 0.30} and its last symbol (now 830001.BJ, which is also the unlisted_days target) picks up BSE lot rules. No test pinned the old numbers, which is why the suite is green, but any future tradable-backtest assertion written against the `store` fixture will see the new values.
- write_daily_fields writes the .npy files before meta.json with no temp-dir-and-rename, so an interrupted call leaves a readable half-built directory. Only a test helper; the design puts the atomic-rename requirement on scripts/build_daily_fields.py (WP9), so this is fine as is.
- conftest's daily_root fixture spins a full 10x60x241 synthetic cube (n_minutes defaults to 241) purely to obtain index-arithmetic planes. Harmless, ~10 MB transient, once per session.
- tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py:336 (_WP3_SYMBOLS, WP2's file) predicts "12 main + 3 specials"; the shipped scheme is "n-3 main + 3 specials", so for n_symbols=12 the real fixture is 9 main + 3 specials. Dead constant, no breakage, but it no longer mirrors WP3.

DEVIATIONS RE-CHECKED AGAINST SOURCE: both of the implementer's declared deviations hold. (1) The ts_delta precision claim: the design's direction is indeed wrong — float32 spacing is ~1.9e-6 at log(1e12)≈27.6 against a ~1e-3 log-return (~2e-3 relative), versus ~1.3e-4 relative for the raw difference at 1e12, so FloatCap wins by ~15x; the test pins the measured direction and dailyfields.py's module docstring already carries the numbers. (2) The test_store_layouts.py edit is forced and minimal. One deviation is MISSING from the list: the ListAge anchoring (defect 1), where the implementation follows the design's "resolve against the view's labels" sentence and silently contradicts its "already listed on the store's first day" sentence.
